summary: James Irving Manatt (1845–1915) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. Educated at Grinnell and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, he held posts at Denison, Marietta, and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln before serving as Professor at Brown University (~1892–1915).

James Ishmael Ford (b. 1948) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Sonoma State and Pacific School of Religion, and trained under Sojun Mel Weitsman, Jiyu-Kennett, and John Tarrant. He founded Boundless Way Zen and Empty Moon Zen Network.

James Kenneth Powell II is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Northwestern, Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD, 1998). His teachers included David Tracy, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

James L. Fitzgerald (b. 1948) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Edwin Gerow and J. A. B. van Buitenen, and held professorial posts at the University of Tennessee and Brown University.
James Legge (1815–1897) was a Sinologist who studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen, and Highbury College. In 1876, he became a Professor at the University of Oxford.

James Luther Adams (1901–1994) worked in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at the University of Minnesota, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University, he held a post at Harvard University from ~1956 to 1968.

James Mackintosh (1765–1832) was a scholar of history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology who studied at the University of Aberdeen and University of Edinburgh. He founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, serving as its president from ~1804 to 1811.

James Mallinson (b. 1970) is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at SOAS and Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He lectured at SOAS (2013) before becoming Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford in 2023.

James Mark Shields (b. 1971) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 2016, he was an Associate Professor at Bucknell University and an Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
James Matthew Baskind specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Yale University, attested in 2006, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Stanley Weinstein.

James McHugh is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard under supervisors including Lawrence McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil, he has held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Southern California.

James Miller is a scholar in Sinology and religious studies who earned an MA at Cambridge (1997) and a PhD at Boston University (2000). In 2014, he was attested as Professor of Chinese Studies and Religious Studies at Queen's University Belfast.
James Morison was an Indology scholar who studied under Georg Bühler. He served as Librarian at the Indian Institute, Oxford (attested 1917) and at the University of Oxford (attested 1920).

James Murdoch (1856–1921) was a Japanology and history scholar who studied at Aberdeen and under Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1889–1893), Kanazawa University (~1898–1901), and Kagoshima University (~1901–1908).

James Prinsep (1799–1840) was an Indologist and historian. He worked at the Benares and Kolkata Mints, was elected a Royal Society Fellow (1828), led The Asiatic Society (1832–1838), and founded the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal and Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum.

James R. Ballantyne (1813–1864) worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. Educated at Edinburgh and under James Michael and Francis Johnson, he served as master at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy, Principal at Benares Sanskrit College, and librarian at the India Office.

James Robson (b. 1965) is a Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies scholar educated at UC Santa Barbara and Stanford. He held posts at Williams, Michigan, and Harvard, becoming Harvard-Yenching Institute director in 2024.

James Smith Reid (1846–1926) was an archaeology and history scholar educated at the University of Cambridge (~1865–1869). He held college posts at Christ's (1869–1880), Pembroke (1873–1885), and Gonville and Caius (1878–1926).

James Sutherland Cotton (1847–1918) was an Indology and history scholar. He studied at Winchester College and Trinity College, Oxford, and held posts from 1871 to 1874 at Queen's College, Benares, and Queens' College, Cambridge.

James Tod (1782–1835) was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar educated at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich, and taught by Gyanchandra. He served with the East India Company (~1799–1823) and was Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1835).
